epics.title: intake: M0 Foundations
goals: FakeJev, the parse pipeline and the intake HTTP API skeleton run and emit valid parse_result (intake-01)
Ticket-note eval set and scorer exist; wrong-without-question is the headline metric
Normalized-note parse cache works offline after the first parse
Vendor spikes written up: Jev (OQ-5), Cartesia Ink, Apify

epics.title: intake: M1 Vertical Slice
goals: Question flow with the send gate: /send refuses any draft with an open question (invariant 3)
Send writes ticket, ticket_constraint and ticket_exception through StateClient
Amendments write revision + 1 with the full constraint set (invariant 9)
Bin profiling and chef confirmation on FakeJev write bin_profile
Intake runs in the platform e2e harness and against a real local SpacetimeDB

epics.title: intake: M2 Live on Pi
goals: Intake service runs on the demo LAN against live SpacetimeDB
Shift-start profiling workflow run with real bin labels
Latency budgets met: parse <= 3 s online, <= 50 ms cached

epics.title: intake: M3 Models
goals: Real Jev adapter scores the eval set at the owner's threshold with zero wrong constraints above threshold
Jev bin profiling from label photos and prep sheets, unclear items routed to chef confirmation
Cartesia Ink live behind Transcriber; transcript confirmed by the server before parsing

epics.title: intake: M4 Demo Hardening
goals: Offline mode: warm cache and manual-entry fallback with no internet
Failure drill: Jev down leads to questions or manual entry, never a guess
Optional: Apify menu import seeds prep sheets

tasks.title: intake: FakeJev, parse pipeline and HTTP API skeleton
tasks.goal: A runnable intake service where POST /v1/parse turns a note into a valid parse_result using a deterministic FakeJev, and every other intake endpoint exists with its contract shape.
acceptance: FakeJev implements JevClient.parse_note with a keyword parser covering the nine allergen units, severity words and 'traces'/'fine' phrasing: `uv run --package intake pytest components/intake -k fake_jev` passes
Pipeline normalizes the note, calls JevClient, and adds a question for every field below question_threshold: `pytest -k pipeline_questions` passes
POST /v1/parse returns JSON that validates against parse_result.schema.json for every note in tests/fixtures/notes_smoke.jsonl: `pytest -k api_parse_contract` passes
All other endpoints in contracts/apis.md#intake-http-api exist and return 501 with the standard error body: `pytest -k api_stubs` passes

Example responses for /v1/parse (ok, with questions) are written to components/intake/fakes/http/ and validate: `python3 tools/validate_contracts.py` still passes and `pytest -k http_fakes_valid` passes
README documents how to run the service locally and the HTTP framework choice
out_of_scope: Any real Jev or vendor call

tasks.title: intake: Build the ticket-note eval set and scorer
tasks.goal: A labeled set of at least 60 ticket notes with expected constraints and exceptions, plus a scorer that reports per-field accuracy and the count of wrong constraints that were not turned into questions.
acceptance: components/intake/eval/notes.jsonl has >= 60 notes, each with expected constraints, exceptions and an 'ambiguous' flag where a question is the right answer

Hard cases covered and tagged: 'no nuts' (peanut ambiguity), 'dairy-free but butter ok', negation ('not allergic to eggs'), misspellings ('seseme'), voice transcription errors ('says me' for sesame), multiple allergens in one note, severity words, 'traces are fine'
Scorer `uv run --package intake intake-eval` prints per-field accuracy and wrong_without_question, and exits non-zero when wrong_without_question > 0
Scorer runs against FakeJev once intake-01 lands; until then it is tested on a trivial stub parser: `pytest -k eval_scorer` passes
Every expected allergen ID exists in contracts/allergen_units.json: `pytest -k eval_units_known` passes
out_of_scope: Tuning FakeJev to pass the whole set

tasks.title: intake: Spike: verify what backs Jev and how to call it
tasks.goal: Answer OQ-5 for Jev as far as agents can: what model or service backs it, how to call it, cost, latency, offline story, and an adapter sketch for JevClient. Anything only the owner can supply goes to status:needs-human.
acceptance: components/intake/docs/jev-spike.md answers: provider or model, auth, request/response shape, rate limits, cost per parse, observed or documented latency, offline options, and whether image input works for bin labels
Every claim cites its source (doc link or owner comment); unverified claims are marked as such
A proposed real-adapter design that keeps the JevClient signature unchanged, and lists the confidence signal Jev can give per field
Questions for the owner are posted on the issue and the issue moves to status:needs-human if keys or a choice are needed
out_of_scope: Committing keys or sample responses containing keys

tasks.title: intake: Spike: verify Cartesia Ink and Apify menu import
tasks.goal: Document how Cartesia Ink speech-to-text and an Apify Actor for menu import would be called, so the Transcriber adapter and /v1/menu/import can be built later without guesswork.
acceptance: components/intake/docs/vendor-spike.md covers, for Cartesia Ink: auth, audio formats, streaming vs batch, latency, cost, offline behavior; for Apify: which Actor, input/output shape, cost, run time
Every claim cites its source; unverified claims are marked
Adapter sketches keep the Transcriber signature and the /v1/menu/import contract unchanged
Owner questions posted on the issue (keys, accounts) with status:needs-human if needed

tasks.title: intake: Add normalized-note parse cache with offline fallback
tasks.goal: Cache parse results by normalized note so a repeated note parses instantly and works offline, and make a cache miss with Jev unavailable fail clearly instead of guessing.
acceptance: Normalization rules (case, whitespace, punctuation, unicode) documented and unit-tested: `pytest -k normalize` passes
Second parse of the same note returns cached=true in <= 50 ms and survives a service restart: `pytest -k cache_hit_persists` passes
JevUnavailable with a cache hit returns the cached result: `pytest -k cache_offline_hit` passes
JevUnavailable with no cache hit returns error code jev_unavailable and writes nothing: `pytest -k cache_offline_miss -m safety` passes
Cache key includes parser name and version so a parser upgrade never serves stale results: `pytest -k cache_versioned` passes

tasks.title: intake: Implement question answers and the send gate
tasks.goal: Answers fill their target fields, sendable flips only when every question is answered, and /send refuses any draft with an open question (invariant 3).
acceptance: POST /v1/drafts/{id}/answers fills the targeted constraint, exception or new constraint and returns an updated parse_result that validates: `pytest -k answers_fill_target` passes
POST /v1/drafts/{id}/send returns 409 unanswered_questions while any question is open: `pytest -k send_gate -m safety` passes

Property test (hypothesis): for arbitrary JevClient outputs, every field below question_threshold has a question after the pipeline runs, and send is refused until all are answered: `pytest -k send_gate_property -m safety` passes
Answering with a value not among the question's options returns 422: `pytest -k answers_invalid_option` passes
Example responses for answers and the 409 error are added to fakes/http/: `pytest -k http_fakes_valid` passes

tasks.title: intake: Apply sent tickets to state via StateClient
tasks.goal: A successful send writes the ticket, its constraints and exceptions through StateClient.put_ticket, with the pass threshold set from the strictest severity on the ticket.
acceptance: Send calls put_ticket with a Ticket that validates against ticket.schema.json: `pytest -k apply_contract` passes against InMemoryStateClient
Default threshold comes from the strictest severity using the OQ-4 defaults in one config object, logged at startup: `pytest -k apply_threshold_default` passes
StateUnavailable on put_ticket returns an error to the caller and the draft stays unsent: `pytest -k apply_state_down -m safety` passes
Sending the same draft twice does not create two tickets: `pytest -k apply_idempotent` passes
Example response for a successful send added to fakes/http/

tasks.title: intake: Support ticket amendments at revision + 1
tasks.goal: POST /v1/tickets/{id}/amend opens a new draft at revision + 1 that goes through the same question flow, and sending it writes a new revision with the full constraint set (invariant 9).
acceptance: Amend returns a parse_result draft pre-filled with the previous revision's constraints plus the new note's: `pytest -k amend_draft` passes
Sending the amendment writes revision + 1 with the complete constraint set; previous revision rows are untouched: `pytest -k amend_revision -m safety` passes
An amendment can never remove a constraint without an explicit answered question confirming the removal: `pytest -k amend_no_silent_drop -m safety` passes
Example responses added to fakes/http/
out_of_scope: Triggering the recheck (provenance subscribes to ticket revisions)

tasks.title: intake: Bin profiling and chef confirmation on FakeJev
tasks.goal: Shift-start bin profiling through POST /v1/profiles/bins and chef confirmation through /confirm, writing bin_profile and opening chef confirmations for unclear ingredients.
acceptance: FakeJev.profile_bin returns an allergen_profile from label or prep-sheet text: `pytest -k profile_bin_fake` passes
POST /v1/profiles/bins writes bin_profile via StateClient.put_bin_profile and returns a valid allergen_profile: `pytest -k profiles_api_contract` passes
Each unclear ingredient opens one chef confirmation; /confirm updates the profile and sets confirmed_by_chef when none remain: `pytest -k chef_confirm_flow` passes
StateClient has no chef-confirmation methods yet: a type:rfc issue is filed for platform/state to add them, and this task uses a local adapter behind a TODO linked to that RFC
Example responses added to fakes/http/

tasks.title: intake: Run intake against a real local SpacetimeDB
tasks.goal: Prove the send and profiling paths work with the real StateClient against a local SpacetimeDB, not only the in-memory fake.
acceptance: An integration test (marked slow) sends a ticket and reads it back through the real StateClient: `uv run --package intake pytest components/intake -m slow -k real_state` passes locally with the state team's documented setup
README documents the env vars needed to point intake at a local SpacetimeDB
PR body includes the command output from a local run
out_of_scope: Running SpacetimeDB in CI unless platform already supports it

tasks.title: intake: Add Transcriber fake and /v1/transcribe endpoint
tasks.goal: Voice tickets work end to end on a fake: /v1/transcribe returns text from TextFileTranscriber, and voice-source notes go through the same parse and question flow.
acceptance: TextFileTranscriber implements Transcriber and returns canned transcripts keyed by audio fixture: `pytest -k transcriber_fake` passes
POST /v1/transcribe accepts audio/wav and returns {"text": ...}: `pytest -k api_transcribe` passes
A note parsed with source=voice yields parse_result.source == 'voice': `pytest -k parse_voice_source` passes
Example responses added to fakes/http/
